item.description: Wearable interfaces that capture both weak physiological fluctuations and large body motions remain difficult to realize in a single fiber because most strain-sensing fibers are governed by one dominant electromechanical response mode. item.description: Neuromodulators such as dopamine (DA) operate through volume transmission in the brain, creating spatially distributed fields that shape circuit excitability. item.description: Unraveling the microscopic origins of non-Fermi liquid behavior near a quantum critical point (QCP) remains a central puzzle in condensed matter physics. item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Gefurulimab in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: The PREVAIL Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Gefurulimab demonstrated both early and sustained clinical benefit in AChR-Ab+ gMG and was well tolerated, supporting its potential as a convenient, once-weekly, self-administered treatment regimen.

item.title: Informal caregiving and leisure satisfaction among middle-aged married women in South Korea: The mediating role of leisure sufficiency
item.description: This study investigated the association between informal caregiving and leisure satisfaction among middle-aged married women in South Korea, with a particular focus on the mediating role of perceived leisure sufficiency. We used nationally representative data from the Korean Longitudinal Survey of Women and Families to classify women in their 40s and 50s into childcare, parental care, and dual-care groups. item.title: Low-Temperature All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description: Reliable battery operation in sub-zero environments is critical for polar exploration, military missions, and space applications. item.title: In situ urethroplasty at the time of artificial urinary sphincter explantation for urethral erosion: an 18-year single-center experience
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Immediate in situ urethroplasty at the time of artificial urinary sphincter explantation was associated with a low observed urethral stricture rate in this selected cohort, although interpretation is limited by the small sample size and absence of a comparator group.

item.description: Background/Objectives: Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation is used to guide bronchoscopes toward peripheral pulmonary lesions, but broad clinical and research adoption remains limited by the cost of proprietary software and by segmentation failures in small distal airways that can interrupt path planning. item.title: Beyond PrEP: The Imperative for an HIV Vaccine to End the Epidemic in Africa
item.description: The era of highly effective pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has transformed HIV prevention, yet global HIV incidence remains unacceptably high, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. While antiretroviral-based prevention is critical, persistent structural barriers to access and adherence highlight the urgent need for a complementary preventive HIV vaccine. item.title: Development of DuoChol, a Thermostable Inactivated Whole-Cell/B-Subunit Oral Cholera Vaccine in Enteric Capsule
item.description: Background/Objectives: Cholera remains an important global health problem. Inactivated oral cholera vaccines (OCVs) are essential in the WHO/GTFCC (World Health Organization/Global Task Force on Cholera Control) strategy to end cholera by 2030; however, global supply is insufficient, they require partial cold-chain storage, and their formulation and antigen contents leave room for improvement. item.title: Immunogenicity of an Oil-in-Water Emulsion Containing Hafnia Alvei-Derived Lipopolysaccharide, with TLR4 and Dectin-2 Agonist Activity In Vitro
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: H. alvei-derived LPS exhibits TLR4 and Dectin-2 agonist activity in vitro. When synergized with an O/W emulsion delivery system, it provides a preliminary indication of cross-species stimulatory potential and supports further investigation as a hypothesis-generating platform for future vaccine adjuvant development.

item.title: Real-World Safety of Concurrent Measles-Mumps-Rubella and Varicella Vaccination in Korean Infants: A Multicenter Self-Controlled Case Series Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Concurrent administration of MMR and varicella vaccines in Korean infants-predominantly using the MAV/06 strain-was associated only with expected, transient increases in fever during days 7-13 postvaccination. No serious or sustained safety signals were identified, supporting the continued use of Korea's separate-injection MMR + V strategy.

item.description: Myrmecochory is a form of seed dispersal mediated by ants. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that even perioperative administration of a single-class antimicrobial agent could be related to the decrease of the gut microbiome diversity with potentially unfavorable taxonomic changes and lead to an increase in ARGs.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: By integrating controlled biomechanical forces with fluid-dynamic airway optimization, RAMPA therapy acts as a mechanotherapeutic modulator. item.description: Bile duct tumor thrombus (BDTT) is a rare manifestation of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that causes obstructive jaundice and is associated with a poor prognosis, although a treatment algorithm has yet to be established. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Age, Constant score, and preoperative differences in scaption and external rotation muscle strength deficits between the injured and uninjured sides are significant predictors of rotator cuff retear after repair surgery. Because MRI is often unavailable, muscle strength measurement offers a practical indirect indicator for retear risk.

Settleable atmospheric particulate matter (SePM), a complex mixture of metals and metalloids, is an emerging stressor in aquatic systems and may interfere with regulatory processes. item.title: First recording of cardiac activity in the Anteos menippe bubble and isoflurane interference during anesthetic induction and recovery
item.description: Understanding the physiological regulation of cardiac activity in insects remains a central topic in insect biochemistry and physiology. In Lepidoptera, direct electrophysiological characterization of cardiac function is still limited, particularly under anesthetic conditions commonly used during experimental manipulation. In this study, we evaluated the effects of isoflurane anesthesia on cardiac electrophysiology in adult Anteos menippe butterflies during anesthetic induction and recovery. A...

item.title: Arthroscopic versus open excision of dorsal wrist ganglia : A comparative study of clinical and recurrence detected by ultrasound
item.description: CONCLUSION: Arthroscopic and open excision yielded comparable clinical outcomes in this cohort. Ultrasound detected a higher frequency of recurrence, particularly after open excision. The clinical relevance of these findings requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

item.title: Hydrogel systems in orthopedics: delivery modality as a framework for translational design
item.description: Orthopedic diseases impose heterogeneous therapeutic demands, ranging from symptomatic control of inflammation and pain to intra-articular drug delivery, cartilage repair, bone regeneration, and prevention of implant-associated infection. item.title: Centriolar Protein POC5 Regulates Human Adipogenesis and Cellular Senescence: Insights From a Novel Metabolic Ciliopathy
item.description: Centrosomes and primary cilia regulate cellular processes, including microtubule organization and lineage-specific differentiation. POC5, a core component of the centriolar inner scaffold, has been linked to syndromic ciliopathies, yet its role in adipose biology remains unclear. This study investigates the impact of POC5 deficiency on ciliary organization, cellular senescence, adipogenesis, and insulin signaling. item.title: Exploring factors that influence the implementation of presurgical smoking cessation interventions: a cross-sectional survey
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The level of implementation of smoking cessation in preoperative visits was poor. The main barriers detected were lack of knowledge and lack of resources and organizational support. Hospitals should promote strategies that address the main barriers identified and should apply interventions to help people quit smoking as a routine practice in preoperative visits.

item.description: The optimal robotic approach for pulmonary segmentectomy remains debated, and objective standards to verify anatomical precision are lacking. item.title: Highly Conserved Core Residues Define Old-World Alphaviruses and Trace Early Evolutionary Divergence
item.description: Alphaviruses are positive-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses that assemble into striking double-icosahedral particles. During budding, the nucleocapsid core forms in the cytoplasm and adopts a T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, a hallmark characteristic of Alphaviruses. item.title: Transfer learning prediction of 2-year native liver survival in biliary atresia following Kasai portoenterostomy using early perioperative biochemical data up to 3 months postoperatively
item.description: CONCLUSION: Early perioperative biochemical data-driven ML models, enhanced by transfer learning, enable accurate prediction of 2-year NLS in BA. GGT_3M, ALB_3M, DBIL_3M, DBIL_1M, and GLO_1W are among the most influential predictors for 2-year NLS after KPE procedure.

item.title: Evaluating Cobas<sup>®</sup> b101 for lipid profile and SCORE2 risk assessment from capillary blood in population screening
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the use of Cobas^(®) b101 with capillary sampling for population-level screening and preliminary CVD risk assessment using SCORE2, despite reduced analytical performance for TG. Abnormal results should be confirmed by a fasting lipid profile.

item.title: Reprogramming of host energy metabolism mediated by the TNF-iNOS-HIF-1α axis plays a key role in host resistance to Plasmodium infection
item.description: TNF has a dual effect in Plasmodium infection, bolstering the host's immune defense while also inducing sickness behavior. Here, we confirm that TNF signaling hampers physical activity, food intake, and energy expenditure while enhancing glucose uptake by the liver and spleen, as well as controlling parasitemia in Plasmodium chabaudi (Pc)-infected mice. item.title: Preserved contextual modulation of eye movements in psychosis prone individuals
item.description: The framework of predictive processing conceives perception as the integration of prior predictions and sensory data. An important source of priors is contextual information, including semantic context (i.e., the meaningful relationships between objects) and temporal context (i.e., the information provided by recent perceptual experiences). item.title: Anteroplacement of the Mucocutaneous Junction and Goblet Cell Expansion: Microanatomic Remodeling of the Human Eyelid Margin
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that conjunctivalization, accompanied by palpebral GC expansion at the MCJ and MGO, may be a function of age-related MCJ anteroplacement. MCJ anteroplacement and reorganization of the MG provides a plausible histopathological link among lid margin anatomy, MG morphology, and ocular surface ecology.

item.title: Cerebral Malaria in Childhood Is Associated With Decreased Long-Term Health-Related Quality of Life
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CM and, to a lesser extent, SMA in childhood are associated with long-term reduction in HRQoL. The chronic effects extend beyond cognition and behavior to affect overall HRQoL.
